mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 2% signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces expected equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% in a consecutive month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS > 2% for 3 consecutive months, or 5-day returns fail to deviate from zero mean in the tightening regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) while UNRATE falls indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite consistent labor strength (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE decline > 0.2%) over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) accompanied by a decline in RSAFS (durable goods orders) suggests strong consumer demand without supply constraints, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% month-over-month while RSAFS decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when GDPC1 is strong and RSAFS is weak.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 105 suggests supply-side weakness, lowering business confidence and equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO shows steady or improving growth for 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5% for two consecutive months in a non-recessionary regime, it signals accommodative policy, lowering real rates and supporting equity valuations, resulting in positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1.5% for two consecutive months and macro regime is non-recessionary
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically positive when FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% within 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% while HOUST (housing starts) rises suggests a labor market softening that dampens consumer spending and equity risk, predicting negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% while HOUST increases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite UNRATE < 3.5% and HOUST growth > 1% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 and PAYEMS exceeding 2% signal a robust demand environment, which elevates equity risk premia and yields positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 2% and PAYEMS > 2% in the same month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive when demand proxies show no consistent trend.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO followed by a sustained drop in RSAFS (both in the same month) indicates supply-side stress, which elevates uncertainty and produces negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 105 and RSAFS < 500,000 in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when INDPRO and RSAFS show simultaneous improvement for 2 months.
